tarsus_1140.name: Tarsus
tarsus_1140.what: A major city of Cilicia in Asia Minor and the birthplace of the apostle Paul.
key: The Lord tells Ananias to seek a man of Tarsus named Saul (Acts 9).
Believers send Saul away to Tarsus after Jews in Jerusalem seek to kill him (Acts 9).
Barnabas goes to Tarsus to find Saul and brings him to Antioch (Acts 11).
Paul tells the Roman tribune he is a citizen of Tarsus, no obscure city (Acts 21).
Paul tells the Jerusalem crowd he was born in Tarsus but raised in Jerusalem (Acts 22).

thebes_1156.name: Thebes
thebes_1156.what: A great ancient capital of Upper Egypt and center of the worship of the god Amon.
key: The Lord announces he will punish Amon of Thebes along with Pharaoh and Egypt (Jeremiah 46).
Ezekiel prophesies that God will execute judgments on Thebes and cut off its multitude (Ezekiel 30).
Nahum warns Nineveh that mighty Thebes was still carried into exile (Nahum 3).

tubal_1183.name: Tubal
tubal_1183.what: A distant nation descended from Japheth, often paired with Meshech, known for trading slaves and bronze.
tubal_1183.today: Likely central or eastern Anatolia, in modern Turkey.
key: God will send survivors to distant nations, including Tubal, to declare his glory (Isaiah 66).
Tubal traded slaves and bronze vessels with the merchants of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Gog is called chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and God declares himself against him (Ezekiel 38).
God promises to defeat Gog, prince of Meshech and Tubal, on the mountains of Israel (Ezekiel 39).

valley_of_achor_1196.name: Valley of Achor
valley_of_achor_1196.what: A valley near Jericho where Achan was executed, later named in prophecy as a place of hope.
valley_of_achor_1196.today: Possibly el-Buqei'a, west of the northern Dead Sea.
key: Achan and his household are stoned in the Valley of Achor for taking devoted things (Joshua 7).
The Valley of Achor marks part of Judah's northern boundary (Joshua 15).
God promises the Valley of Achor will become a resting place for herds (Isaiah 65).
God promises to make the Valley of Achor a door of hope for Israel (Hosea 2).

zeboiim_1244.name: Zeboiim
zeboiim_1244.what: One of the cities of the plain near Sodom and Gomorrah, destroyed in God's judgment.
zeboiim_1244.today: Exact site unknown; probably near the southern Dead Sea.
key: Zeboiim is listed near Sodom and Gomorrah on the edge of Canaanite territory (Genesis 10).
Shemeber king of Zeboiim joins the kings of the valley against Chedorlaomer (Genesis 14).
Moses warns that disobedience could leave the land like Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew (Deuteronomy 29).
God asks how he could make Israel like Zeboiim, showing his compassion (Hosea 11).

ain_42.name: Ain
ain_42.what: A town in the far south of Judah, later assigned to Simeon and listed as a Levitical city.
ain_42.today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev near Rimmon, southern Israel.
key: Ain is listed among the southernmost towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Ain is allotted to the tribe of Simeon within Judah's territory (Joshua 19).
Ain is given to the Levites as one of their cities (Joshua 21).
Ain appears among the towns where the descendants of Simeon lived (1 Chronicles 4).

antioch_69.name: Pisidian Antioch
antioch_69.what: A Roman colony in the region of Pisidia in Asia Minor, visited by Paul on his first missionary journey.
antioch_69.today: Ruins near Yalvac, in west-central Turkey.
key: Paul preaches in the synagogue, and many Gentiles believe, but Jews drive him out (Acts 13).
Jews from Antioch stir up crowds in Lystra, who stone Paul (Acts 14).
Paul and Barnabas return to strengthen the disciples in Antioch (Acts 14).
Paul reminds Timothy of the persecutions he endured at Antioch (2 Timothy 3).

arad_81.name: Arad
arad_81.what: A Canaanite royal city in the Negev whose king attacked Israel in the wilderness.
arad_81.today: Tel Arad, in the northeastern Negev, Israel.
key: The king of Arad attacks Israel, and Israel devotes his cities to destruction (Numbers 21).
The Canaanite king of Arad hears that Israel is coming (Numbers 33).
The king of Arad is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
The Kenites settle among the people in the Negev near Arad (Judges 1).

argob_88.name: Argob
argob_88.what: A region of Bashan with sixty fortified cities, taken from Og king of Bashan.
argob_88.today: In Bashan, southern Syria; exact extent uncertain.
key: Israel captures the sixty cities of Argob from Og king of Bashan (Deuteronomy 3).
Jair of Manasseh takes the region of Argob and names it after himself (Deuteronomy 3).
Argob falls within the district of Solomon's officer Ben-geber (1 Kings 4).

ashan_100.name: Ashan
ashan_100.what: A town in the lowland of Judah, later allotted to Simeon and given to the priests.
ashan_100.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly near Beersheba, southern Israel.
key: Ashan is listed among the towns of the lowland of Judah (Joshua 15).
Ashan is allotted to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19).
Ashan appears among the towns where Simeon's descendants lived (1 Chronicles 4).
Ashan is given with its pasturelands to the descendants of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6).

asshur_109.name: Asshur
asshur_109.what: The ancient heartland of Assyria and its first capital, often standing for the Assyrian nation.
asshur_109.today: Qal'at Sherqat, on the Tigris River in northern Iraq.
key: Balaam foretells that Asshur will take the Kenites captive and later be afflicted (Numbers 24).
The psalmist names Asshur among nations conspiring against God's people (Psalms 83).
Merchants of Asshur trade fine garments with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

beth-horon_733.name: Lower Beth-horon
beth-horon_733.what: The lower of two towns guarding the ascent from the coastal plain toward the hill country northwest of Jerusalem.
beth-horon_733.today: Beit Ur et-Tahta, northwest of Jerusalem, West Bank.
key: Lower Beth-horon marks the boundary of the descendants of Joseph (Joshua 16).
Lower Beth-horon lies on the border of Benjamin's territory (Joshua 18).
Solomon rebuilds Lower Beth-horon (1 Kings 9).
Solomon fortifies Upper and Lower Beth-horon with walls, gates, and bars (2 Chronicles 8).

beth-jeshimoth_215.name: Beth-jeshimoth
beth-jeshimoth_215.what: A town on the plains of Moab near the Jordan, at the edge of Israel's last wilderness camp.
beth-jeshimoth_215.today: Likely Tell el-Azeimeh, northeast of the Dead Sea, Jordan.
key: Israel camps along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim (Numbers 33).
Beth-jeshimoth marks a boundary of the kingdom of Sihon (Joshua 12).
Beth-jeshimoth is allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).
Ezekiel names Beth-jeshimoth among Moab's glorious cities facing judgment (Ezekiel 25).

beth-peor_228.name: Beth-peor
beth-peor_228.what: A town in Moab near Mount Nebo, opposite the valley where Israel camped and Moses was buried.
beth-peor_228.today: Exact site unknown; near Mount Nebo in Jordan.
key: Israel remains in the valley opposite Beth-peor (Deuteronomy 3).
Moses sets the law before Israel in the valley opposite Beth-peor (Deuteronomy 4).
God buries Moses in a valley opposite Beth-peor, and his grave remains unknown (Deuteronomy 34).
Beth-peor is allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).

bezer_247.name: Bezer
bezer_247.what: A city of refuge on the tableland east of the Jordan in the territory of Reuben.
bezer_247.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Umm el-Amad, near Madaba, Jordan.
key: Moses sets apart Bezer as a city of refuge for Reuben (Deuteronomy 4).
Bezer is confirmed as one of the six cities of refuge (Joshua 20).
Bezer is given to the Levites of the clan of Merari (Joshua 21).
Bezer is listed again among the Merarite Levitical cities (1 Chronicles 6).

brook_eshcol_1202.name: Valley of Eshcol
brook_eshcol_1202.what: A valley near Hebron where the twelve spies cut a huge cluster of grapes.
brook_eshcol_1202.today: Near Hebron, West Bank; exact site unknown.
key: The spies cut a cluster of grapes so large two men carry it on a pole (Numbers 13).
Moses recalls that the spies saw Eshcol yet discouraged Israel from entering the land (Numbers 32).
Moses retells how the spies reached the Valley of Eshcol and brought back fruit (Deuteronomy 1).

cana_271.name: Cana
cana_271.what: A village in Galilee where Jesus performed his first sign, turning water into wine.
cana_271.today: Likely Khirbet Qana, north of Nazareth, Israel.
key: Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding, his first sign (John 2).
At Cana Jesus heals an official's son who lies sick in Capernaum (John 4).
Nathanael of Cana is among the disciples who meet the risen Jesus (John 21).

chephirah_285.name: Chephirah
chephirah_285.what: One of four Gibeonite cities that made a treaty with Joshua, later part of Benjamin.
chephirah_285.today: Khirbet el-Kefireh, west of Jerusalem, Israel.
key: Chephirah is one of the Gibeonite cities spared through Israel's treaty (Joshua 9).
Chephirah is allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18).
Men of Chephirah return from exile in Babylon (Ezra 2).
The returnees from Chephirah are listed again (Nehemiah 7).

derbe_330.name: Derbe
derbe_330.what: A city of Lycaonia in Asia Minor where Paul preached on his missionary journeys.
derbe_330.today: Likely Kerti Huyuk, near Karaman, south-central Turkey.
key: Paul and Barnabas preach in Derbe and make many disciples after Paul is stoned (Acts 14).
Paul returns to Derbe and Lystra, where he meets Timothy (Acts 16).
Gaius of Derbe travels with Paul toward Jerusalem (Acts 20).

dor_341.name: Dor
dor_341.what: A Canaanite port city on the Mediterranean coast south of Mount Carmel.
dor_341.today: Tel Dor, on the coast south of Haifa, Israel.
key: The king of Dor is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Dor is given to Manasseh, but the Canaanites remain there (Joshua 17).
Manasseh fails to drive out the inhabitants of Dor (Judges 1).
Dor is listed among the towns held by the descendants of Joseph (1 Chronicles 7).

dung_gate_346.name: Dung Gate
dung_gate_346.what: A gate in the southern wall of ancient Jerusalem, rebuilt in Nehemiah's day.
dung_gate_346.today: Southern end of ancient Jerusalem; not the Old City's modern Dung Gate.
key: Nehemiah inspects the broken walls by night, passing the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 2).
Malchijah son of Rechab repairs the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 3).
One thanksgiving choir marches on the wall toward the Dung Gate at its dedication (Nehemiah 12).

elim_369.name: Elim
elim_369.what: An oasis in the wilderness with twelve springs and seventy palm trees, where Israel camped after the Red Sea.
elim_369.today: Possibly Wadi Gharandel, in western Sinai, Egypt.
key: Israel camps at Elim beside twelve springs and seventy palm trees (Exodus 15).
Israel sets out from Elim into the wilderness of Sin (Exodus 16).
Elim is recorded among Israel's wilderness camps (Numbers 33).

en-rogel_395.name: En-rogel
en-rogel_395.what: A spring just outside Jerusalem where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet.
en-rogel_395.today: Likely Bir Ayyub, just south of the City of David, Jerusalem.
key: En-rogel marks part of Judah's northern boundary (Joshua 15).
En-rogel marks part of Benjamin's southern boundary (Joshua 18).
Jonathan and Ahimaaz wait at En-rogel to carry news to David during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 17).
Adonijah sacrifices near En-rogel while trying to make himself king (1 Kings 1).

etham_417.name: Etham
etham_417.what: A camp on the edge of the wilderness on Israel's route out of Egypt.
etham_417.today: Exact site unknown; on the eastern edge of the Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Israel moves from Succoth and camps at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness (Exodus 13).
Israel camps at Etham and later travels three days in the wilderness of Etham (Numbers 33).

ethiopia_419.name: Cush
ethiopia_419.what: An ancient land south of Egypt, marking the far edge of the known world in biblical times.
ethiopia_419.today: Mainly modern Sudan, south of Egypt; not modern Ethiopia.
key: The river Gihon flows around the whole land of Cush (Genesis 2).
King Ahasuerus rules 127 provinces from India to Cush (Esther 1).
Mordecai's decree goes to every province from India to Cush (Esther 8).
Job says the topaz of Cush cannot equal the worth of wisdom (Job 28).

gaash_429.name: Gaash
gaash_429.what: A mountain in the hill country of Ephraim near Joshua's burial place.
gaash_429.today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country of Ephraim, West Bank.
key: Joshua is buried at Timnath-serah, north of the mountain of Gaash (Joshua 24).
Judges repeats that Joshua was buried north of the mountain of Gaash (Judges 2).
Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash is among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash appears in the list of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

gate_of_benjamin_175.name: Benjamin Gate
gate_of_benjamin_175.what: A gate on the north side of Jerusalem facing the territory of Benjamin.
gate_of_benjamin_175.today: North side of ancient Jerusalem; exact site unknown.
key: Pashhur beats Jeremiah and puts him in the stocks in the upper Benjamin Gate (Jeremiah 20).
Jeremiah is arrested at the Benjamin Gate and accused of deserting to the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 37).
Ebed-melech appeals for Jeremiah while King Zedekiah sits in the Benjamin Gate (Jeremiah 38).
Zechariah foresees Jerusalem restored from the Benjamin Gate to the Corner Gate (Zechariah 14).

golan_486.name: Golan
golan_486.what: A city of refuge in Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, in the territory of Manasseh.
golan_486.today: Possibly Sahem el-Jolan, southern Syria; it gave its name to the Golan Heights.
key: Moses sets apart Golan in Bashan as a city of refuge for Manasseh (Deuteronomy 4).
Golan is confirmed as one of the six cities of refuge (Joshua 20).
Golan is given to the Gershonite Levites (Joshua 21).
Golan is listed again among the Gershonite Levitical cities (1 Chronicles 6).

havvoth-jair_535.name: Havvoth-jair
havvoth-jair_535.what: A group of villages east of the Jordan, named after Jair of the tribe of Manasseh.
havvoth-jair_535.today: In Gilead and Bashan, northern Jordan; exact sites unknown.
key: Jair son of Manasseh captures villages and calls them Havvoth-jair (Numbers 32).
Jair takes the region of Argob and names Bashan's villages Havvoth-jair (Deuteronomy 3).
The judge Jair's thirty sons have thirty cities called Havvoth-jair in Gilead (Judges 10).
Geshur and Aram take Havvoth-jair from Israel (1 Chronicles 2).

hazar-enan_537.name: Hazar-enan
hazar-enan_537.what: A town marking the northeastern corner of the boundary of the promised land.
hazar-enan_537.today: Exact site unknown; possibly in central Syria.
key: The Lord sets Hazar-enan as the end of Israel's northern boundary (Numbers 34).
Ezekiel names Hazar-enan on the northern boundary of the restored land (Ezekiel 47).
Ezekiel again names Hazar-enan at the northern limit of Dan's portion (Ezekiel 48).

hazar-shual_539.name: Hazar-shual
hazar-shual_539.what: A town in the Negev of Judah, later allotted to Simeon and resettled after the exile.
hazar-shual_539.today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev near Beersheba, Israel.
key: Hazar-shual is listed among the southern towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Hazar-shual is allotted to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19).
Hazar-shual appears among the towns where Simeon's descendants lived (1 Chronicles 4).
Men of Judah live in Hazar-shual after the return from exile (Nehemiah 11).

horesh_578.name: Horesh
horesh_578.what: A place in the wilderness of Ziph where David hid from Saul.
horesh_578.today: Possibly Khirbet Khoreisa, south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: David hides at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph while Saul seeks his life (1 Samuel 23).
Jonathan meets David at Horesh and strengthens his hand in God (1 Samuel 23).
The Ziphites tell Saul that David is hiding at Horesh (1 Samuel 23).

horonaim_581.name: Horonaim
horonaim_581.what: A town of Moab named in prophecies of Moab's destruction.
horonaim_581.today: Exact site unknown; in Moab, Jordan.
key: Isaiah describes a cry of destruction on the road to Horonaim (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah foretells the cry of desolation and great destruction from Horonaim (Jeremiah 48).

italy_601.name: Italy
italy_601.what: The Roman peninsula, home of the imperial capital Rome.
key: Aquila and Priscilla have recently come from Italy after Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome (Acts 18).
Paul sails for Italy as a prisoner under the centurion Julius (Acts 27).
Those from Italy send greetings to the letter's readers (Hebrews 13).

jattir_626.name: Jattir
jattir_626.what: A town in the hill country of Judah given to the priests.
jattir_626.today: Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Jattir is listed among the towns of the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
Jattir is given to the descendants of Aaron (Joshua 21).
David sends spoil from the Amalekites to the elders of Jattir (1 Samuel 30).
Jattir is listed again among the priests' cities (1 Chronicles 6).

jeshimon_639.name: Jeshimon
jeshimon_639.what: A barren wasteland in Judah, near which David hid from Saul.
jeshimon_639.today: The Judean wilderness west of the Dead Sea, West Bank.
key: The Ziphites say David hides on the hill of Hachilah, south of Jeshimon (1 Samuel 23).
David stays in the wilderness of Maon, south of Jeshimon (1 Samuel 23).
Saul camps on the hill of Hachilah beside Jeshimon while hunting David (1 Samuel 26).

kedemoth_675.name: Kedemoth
kedemoth_675.what: A town and wilderness east of the Dead Sea, later given to Reuben and the Levites.
kedemoth_675.today: Exact site uncertain; east of the Dead Sea, Jordan.
key: Moses sends messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon asking for passage (Deuteronomy 2).
Kedemoth is allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).
Kedemoth is given to the Merarite Levites (Joshua 21).
Kedemoth is listed again among the Levitical cities (1 Chronicles 6).

kiriath-sepher_703.name: Kiriath-sepher
kiriath-sepher_703.what: The earlier name of Debir, a town in Judah captured by Othniel.
kiriath-sepher_703.today: Debir, possibly Khirbet Rabud, southwest of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Caleb offers his daughter Achsah to whoever captures Kiriath-sepher (Joshua 15).
Othniel captures Kiriath-sepher and marries Achsah (Joshua 15).
Judges retells Othniel's capture of Kiriath-sepher, formerly the name of Debir (Judges 1).

laish_713.name: Laish
laish_713.what: A quiet, isolated city in the far north captured by the tribe of Dan and renamed Dan.
key: Danite spies find the people of Laish quiet, unsuspecting, and far from help (Judges 18).
The Danites strike Laish and burn it (Judges 18).
The Danites rebuild the city and rename Laish as Dan (Judges 18).

lod_731.name: Lod
lod_731.what: A town on the coastal plain of Benjamin, resettled by returning exiles.
lod_731.today: Lod, near Ben Gurion Airport, Israel.
key: Shemed of Benjamin builds Ono and Lod (1 Chronicles 8).
People of Lod, Hadid, and Ono return from exile (Ezra 2).
The returnees of Lod are listed again (Nehemiah 7).
Benjaminites live in Lod after the exile (Nehemiah 11).

lud_735.name: Lud
lud_735.what: A distant nation known for its archers and soldiers, listed among faraway peoples.
lud_735.today: Uncertain; possibly Lydia in western Turkey, or a people in Africa.
key: God will send survivors to Lud and other nations to declare his glory (Isaiah 66).
Men of Lud, skilled archers, serve in Egypt's army (Jeremiah 46).
Men of Lud serve as soldiers in the army of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Lud is named among Egypt's allies who will fall by the sword (Ezekiel 30).

maacah_743.name: Maacah
maacah_743.what: A small Aramean kingdom north of Bashan, near the slopes of Mount Hermon.
maacah_743.today: Around the northern Golan Heights and southern Lebanon.
key: The Ammonites hire the king of Maacah and his men to fight David (2 Samuel 10).
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai of Maacah is among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles records the king of Maacah and his troops joining the Ammonites (1 Chronicles 19).

maon_764.name: Maon
maon_764.what: A town in the hill country of Judah with a nearby wilderness where David hid from Saul.
maon_764.today: Khirbet Ma'in, south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Maon is listed among the towns of the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
Saul pursues David in the wilderness of Maon (1 Samuel 23).
Nabal, Abigail's husband, lives in Maon (1 Samuel 25).

massah_771.name: Massah
massah_771.what: A place near Rephidim where Israel tested the Lord by demanding water.
massah_771.today: Near Rephidim in the Sinai Peninsula; exact site unknown.
key: Israel quarrels and tests the Lord over water, so Moses names the place Massah and Meribah (Exodus 17).
Moses warns Israel not to put the Lord to the test as at Massah (Deuteronomy 6).
Moses recalls that Israel provoked the Lord at Massah (Deuteronomy 9).
Moses' blessing on Levi recalls God testing him at Massah (Deuteronomy 33).

mephaath_780.name: Mephaath
mephaath_780.what: A town on the tableland of Moab, allotted to Reuben and given to the Levites.
mephaath_780.today: Likely Umm er-Rasas, southeast of Madaba, Jordan.
key: Mephaath is allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).
Mephaath is given to the Merarite Levites (Joshua 21).
Mephaath is listed again among the Levitical cities (1 Chronicles 6).
Jeremiah names Mephaath among Moab's cities facing judgment (Jeremiah 48).

meribah_782.name: Meribah
meribah_782.what: The waters at Kadesh where Moses struck the rock and Israel quarreled with the Lord.
meribah_782.today: Near Kadesh-barnea, in the northeastern Sinai Peninsula.
key: Moses strikes the rock, and the waters are named Meribah because Israel quarreled (Numbers 20).
God recalls that Moses and Aaron rebelled at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh (Numbers 27).
God recalls testing Israel at the waters of Meribah (Psalms 81).

moladah_816.name: Moladah
moladah_816.what: A town in the Negev of Judah, later allotted to Simeon and resettled after the exile.
moladah_816.today: Exact site uncertain; in the Negev east of Beersheba, Israel.
key: Moladah is listed among the southern towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Moladah is allotted to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19).
Moladah appears among the towns where Simeon's descendants lived (1 Chronicles 4).
Men of Judah live in Moladah after the return from exile (Nehemiah 11).

mount_gerizim_836.name: Mount Gerizim
mount_gerizim_836.what: A mountain beside Shechem, facing Mount Ebal, where the blessings of the covenant were pronounced.
mount_gerizim_836.today: Jabal at-Tur, above Nablus, West Bank.
key: Moses commands that the blessing be set on Mount Gerizim (Deuteronomy 11).
Six tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people (Deuteronomy 27).
Half of Israel stands before Mount Gerizim as Joshua reads the law (Joshua 8).
Jotham tells his fable of the trees from the top of Mount Gerizim (Judges 9).

mount_of_esau_835.name: Mount Esau
mount_of_esau_835.what: The mountainous homeland of Edom, the nation descended from Esau.
mount_of_esau_835.today: The highlands of Edom, southern Jordan.
key: God declares he will destroy understanding from Mount Esau (Obadiah 1).
Everyone from Mount Esau will be cut off by slaughter (Obadiah 1).
Saviors will go up to Mount Zion to rule Mount Esau, and the kingdom will be the Lord's (Obadiah 1).

oboth_906.name: Oboth
oboth_906.what: A stopping place of Israel near the border of Moab during the wilderness journey.
oboth_906.today: Exact site unknown; south or east of the Dead Sea, Jordan.
key: After the bronze serpent, Israel sets out and camps at Oboth (Numbers 21).
Oboth is recorded among Israel's wilderness camps (Numbers 33).

on_908.name: On
on_908.what: An ancient Egyptian city and center of sun worship, home of Joseph's father-in-law.
key: Pharaoh gives Joseph Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as his wife (Genesis 41).
Asenath of On bears Joseph's sons Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 46).
Ezekiel foretells that the young men of On will fall by the sword (Ezekiel 30).

peor_933.name: Peor
peor_933.what: A mountain in Moab where Balaam was taken and where Israel later worshiped Baal of Peor.
peor_933.today: In Moab near Mount Nebo, Jordan; exact site unknown.
key: Balak takes Balaam to the top of Peor to curse Israel (Numbers 23).
Israel yokes itself to Baal of Peor, and a plague follows (Numbers 25).
Moses says Balaam's advice caused Israel to sin at Peor (Numbers 31).
Phinehas recalls the sin at Peor when confronting the eastern tribes (Joshua 22).

philippi_942.name: Philippi
philippi_942.what: A leading Roman colony in Macedonia and the first place in Europe where Paul planted a church.
key: Lydia believes, a slave girl is freed, and a jailer is converted (Acts 16).
Paul sails from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread (Acts 20).
Paul writes to the saints at Philippi with their overseers and deacons (Philippians 1).
Paul recalls being shamefully treated at Philippi before coming to Thessalonica (1 Thessalonians 2).

pirathon_949.name: Pirathon
pirathon_949.what: A town in the hill country of Ephraim, home of the judge Abdon and David's warrior Benaiah.
pirathon_949.today: Likely Far'ata, southwest of Nablus, West Bank.
key: Abdon the Pirathonite judges Israel and is buried at Pirathon (Judges 12).
Benaiah of Pirathon is among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Benaiah of Pirathon appears in the Chronicler's list of mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).
Benaiah of Pirathon commands David's division for the eleventh month (1 Chronicles 27).

rameses_980.name: Rameses
rameses_980.what: A city and district in the eastern Nile Delta, where Israel lived and from which the exodus began.
rameses_980.today: Likely Qantir, in the eastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Joseph settles his family in the best of the land, the land of Rameses (Genesis 47).
Israel journeys from Rameses to Succoth at the exodus (Exodus 12).
Israel sets out from Rameses the day after the Passover (Numbers 33).

rehob_989.name: Rehob
rehob_989.what: A town in the territory of Asher, later given to the Levites.
rehob_989.today: Exact site uncertain; in western Galilee near Acco, Israel.
key: Rehob is listed within the territory of Asher (Joshua 19).
Rehob is given to the Gershonite Levites (Joshua 21).
Asher fails to drive out the inhabitants of Rehob (Judges 1).
Rehob is listed again among the Levitical cities (1 Chronicles 6).

rimmon_1004.name: Rimmon
rimmon_1004.what: A town in the far south of Judah, later allotted to Simeon.
rimmon_1004.today: Possibly Khirbet Umm er-Ramamin, north of Beersheba, Israel.
key: Rimmon is listed among the southernmost towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Rimmon is allotted to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19).
Rimmon appears among the towns where Simeon's descendants lived (1 Chronicles 4).
Zechariah foresees the land leveled from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem (Zechariah 14).

rock_1011.name: Rock of Escape
rock_1011.what: A rock in the wilderness of Maon where David narrowly escaped Saul.
rock_1011.today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness of Maon, south of Hebron.
key: David goes down to the rock in the wilderness of Maon as Saul closes in (1 Samuel 23).
Saul breaks off pursuit to face a Philistine raid, so the place is called the Rock of Escape (1 Samuel 23).

salecah_1017.name: Salecah
salecah_1017.what: A city on the eastern edge of Bashan, marking the limit of Og's kingdom.
key: Israel takes the cities of Og's kingdom as far as Salecah (Deuteronomy 3).
Og king of Bashan ruled as far as Salecah (Joshua 12).
Salecah marks the eastern limit of the land given east of the Jordan (Joshua 13).
The Gadites live in Bashan as far as Salecah (1 Chronicles 5).

salem_1018.name: Salem
salem_1018.what: The city of Melchizedek, king and priest, generally identified with Jerusalem.
key: Melchizedek king of Salem brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram (Genesis 14).
The psalmist says God's abode has been established in Salem (Psalms 76).
Hebrews explains that king of Salem means king of peace (Hebrews 7).

senir_1047.name: Senir
senir_1047.what: The Amorite name for Mount Hermon or part of its range.
senir_1047.today: Mount Hermon, on the Lebanon-Syria border.
key: Moses notes that the Amorites call Mount Hermon Senir (Deuteronomy 3).
The half-tribe of Manasseh settles from Bashan to Senir and Mount Hermon (1 Chronicles 5).
The bride is called to come down from the peaks of Senir and Hermon (Song of Solomon 4).
Tyre's ship planks are made of fir trees from Senir (Ezekiel 27).

sheep_gate_1070.name: Sheep Gate
sheep_gate_1070.what: A gate in the northern wall of Jerusalem near the temple, beside the pool of Bethesda.
sheep_gate_1070.today: Northeast of the temple area in Jerusalem's Old City; exact site unknown.
key: Eliashib and the priests rebuild and consecrate the Sheep Gate (Nehemiah 3).
The thanksgiving procession passes the Sheep Gate at the wall's dedication (Nehemiah 12).
Jesus heals a man by the pool near the Sheep Gate (John 5).

shittim_1086.name: Shittim
shittim_1086.what: Israel's final camp on the plains of Moab before crossing the Jordan.
shittim_1086.today: Possibly Tell el-Hammam, east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, Jordan.
key: While at Shittim, Israel commits sexual immorality with Moabite women and worships Baal (Numbers 25).
Joshua secretly sends two spies from Shittim to Jericho (Joshua 2).
Israel sets out from Shittim and comes to the Jordan (Joshua 3).
Micah calls Israel to remember what happened from Shittim to Gilgal (Micah 6).

sin_1097.name: Wilderness of Sin
sin_1097.what: A wilderness between Elim and Mount Sinai where God first gave Israel manna and quail.
sin_1097.today: Likely in the southwestern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt; exact site uncertain.
key: Israel grumbles in the wilderness of Sin, and God provides quail and manna (Exodus 16).
Israel moves on from the wilderness of Sin to Rephidim (Exodus 17).
The wilderness of Sin is recorded among Israel's camps (Numbers 33).

succoth_1114.name: Succoth
succoth_1114.what: The first camp of Israel after leaving Rameses at the exodus.
succoth_1114.today: Likely Tell el-Maskhuta, in the eastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: About six hundred thousand men on foot journey from Rameses to Succoth (Exodus 12).
Israel sets out from Succoth and camps at Etham (Exodus 13).
Succoth is recorded as Israel's first camp after Rameses (Numbers 33).

thyatira_1160.name: Thyatira
thyatira_1160.what: A trading city in the Roman province of Asia, home of one of the seven churches of Revelation.
key: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from Thyatira, believes Paul's message in Philippi (Acts 16).
Thyatira is named among the seven churches receiving John's book (Revelation 1).
Jesus commends Thyatira's love and service but rebukes its tolerance of Jezebel (Revelation 2).

tower_1177.name: Tower of Hananel
tower_1177.what: A tower on the northern wall of Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate.
tower_1177.today: North wall of ancient Jerusalem; exact site unknown.
key: The priests rebuild the wall as far as the Tower of Hananel (Nehemiah 3).
The thanksgiving procession passes the Tower of Hananel (Nehemiah 12).
God promises the city will be rebuilt from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate (Jeremiah 31).
Zechariah foresees Jerusalem inhabited from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses (Zechariah 14).

ur_1189.name: Ur
ur_1189.what: A city in southern Mesopotamia, the original home of Abraham's family.
key: Haran dies in Ur, and Terah takes Abram from Ur toward Canaan (Genesis 11).
The Lord reminds Abram that he brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 15).
The Levites praise God for choosing Abram and bringing him out of Ur (Nehemiah 9).

valley_of_salt_1215.name: Valley of Salt
valley_of_salt_1215.what: A valley in the south, near Edom's border, where Judah's armies defeated the Edomites.
valley_of_salt_1215.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly south of the Dead Sea.
key: David strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (2 Samuel 8).
Amaziah strikes down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (2 Kings 14).
Abishai strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (1 Chronicles 18).
Amaziah leads his people to the Valley of Salt and defeats the men of Seir (2 Chronicles 25).

water_gate_1230.name: Water Gate
water_gate_1230.what: A gate on the east side of Jerusalem where Ezra read the Law to the people.
water_gate_1230.today: East side of the City of David, near the Gihon Spring; exact site unknown.
key: Temple servants living on the Ophel repair up to a point opposite the Water Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Ezra reads the Book of the Law to the people in the square before the Water Gate (Nehemiah 8).
The people build booths in the square of the Water Gate for the Feast of Booths (Nehemiah 8).

zarephath_1242.name: Zarephath
zarephath_1242.what: A Phoenician town near Sidon where Elijah stayed with a widow during the drought.
zarephath_1242.today: Sarafand, on the coast of southern Lebanon between Tyre and Sidon.
key: God sends Elijah to a widow in Zarephath, whose flour and oil do not run out (1 Kings 17).
Elijah raises the widow's son to life (1 Kings 17).
Obadiah foresees Israelite exiles possessing the land as far as Zarephath (Obadiah 1).
Jesus notes Elijah was sent only to a widow of Zarephath in Sidon (Luke 4).

abel_4.name: Abel
abel_4.what: A fortified town in the far north of Israel where the rebel Sheba took refuge.
abel_4.today: Tel Abel Beth Maacah, near Metula, northern Israel.
key: Sheba son of Bichri flees to Abel, and Joab besieges the city (2 Samuel 20).
A wise woman of Abel persuades the city to throw Sheba's head to Joab, saving it (2 Samuel 20).

abel-meholah_8.name: Abel-meholah
abel-meholah_8.what: A town in the Jordan Valley and hometown of the prophet Elisha.
abel-meholah_8.today: Exact site uncertain; in the Jordan Valley south of Beth-shean.
key: The fleeing Midianites run toward the border of Abel-meholah after Gideon's attack (Judges 7).
Abel-meholah lies within the district of Solomon's officer Baana (1 Kings 4).
God tells Elijah to anoint Elisha son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah as prophet (1 Kings 19).

achshaph_17.name: Achshaph
achshaph_17.what: A Canaanite royal city in northern Canaan, later on the border of Asher.
achshaph_17.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tell Keisan, near Acco, Israel.
key: Jabin king of Hazor summons the king of Achshaph to fight Israel (Joshua 11).
The king of Achshaph is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Achshaph lies on the boundary of Asher's territory (Joshua 19).

ahava_34.name: Ahava
ahava_34.what: A river or canal in Babylonia where Ezra gathered the returning exiles before traveling to Jerusalem.
ahava_34.today: Exact site unknown; in Babylonia, modern Iraq.
key: Ezra gathers the exiles by the river that runs to Ahava and finds no Levites (Ezra 8).
Ezra proclaims a fast at the river Ahava to seek a safe journey from God (Ezra 8).
The company departs from the river Ahava, and God protects them on the way (Ezra 8).

akrabbim_44.name: Akrabbim
akrabbim_44.what: A steep ascent marking the southern border of the promised land and of Judah.
akrabbim_44.today: Likely Ma'ale Akrabim (Scorpion Pass), in the Negev, southern Israel.
key: The southern boundary of the land runs south of the ascent of Akrabbim (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passes south of the ascent of Akrabbim (Joshua 15).
The Amorites' border runs from the ascent of Akrabbim (Judges 1).

alexandria_46.name: Alexandria
alexandria_46.what: A great Egyptian seaport founded by Alexander the Great, a center of Jewish learning and grain shipping.
alexandria_46.today: Alexandria, on the Mediterranean coast of Egypt.
key: Apollos, a native of Alexandria, comes to Ephesus (Acts 18).
Paul's centurion finds an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and puts them aboard (Acts 27).
After the shipwreck, Paul sails on an Alexandrian ship that wintered at Malta (Acts 28).

aphek_72.name: Aphek
aphek_72.what: A city on the Sharon plain where the Philistines gathered to fight Israel.
aphek_72.today: Tel Aphek, near Rosh HaAyin, central Israel.
key: The king of Aphek is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
The Philistines camp at Aphek and defeat Israel, then capture the ark (1 Samuel 4).
The Philistines gather at Aphek, and David is sent back from their army (1 Samuel 29).

aphek_73.name: Aphek
aphek_73.what: A town east of the Sea of Galilee where Israel defeated the Syrians.
aphek_73.today: Likely near Afik, east of the Sea of Galilee, Golan Heights.
key: Ben-hadad attacks at Aphek, Israel defeats Syria, and a wall falls on survivors (1 Kings 20).
Elisha's arrow of victory promises that Joash will defeat the Syrians in Aphek (2 Kings 13).

areopagus_87.name: Areopagus
areopagus_87.what: A rocky hill in Athens and the name of the council that met there.
areopagus_87.today: A hill northwest of the Acropolis in Athens, Greece.
key: Athenian philosophers bring Paul to the Areopagus to hear his new teaching (Acts 17).
Paul proclaims the unknown god as the Creator who raised Jesus from the dead (Acts 17).
Dionysius the Areopagite and others believe (Acts 17).

ariel_89.name: Ariel
ariel_89.what: A poetic name for Jerusalem, the city where David camped.
key: Isaiah pronounces woe on Ariel, the city where David encamped (Isaiah 29).
God will bring distress on Ariel, and it will be like an altar hearth (Isaiah 29).
The nations fighting against Ariel will vanish like a dream (Isaiah 29).

arimathea_90.name: Arimathea
arimathea_90.what: A town of Judea, home of Joseph, the disciple who buried Jesus.
arimathea_90.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Rentis, northwest of Jerusalem.
key: Joseph of Arimathea, a rich disciple, lays Jesus' body in his own new tomb (Matthew 27).
Joseph, a respected council member, boldly asks Pilate for Jesus' body (Mark 15).
Joseph, a secret disciple, and Nicodemus prepare and bury Jesus' body (John 19).

azmon_130.name: Azmon
azmon_130.what: A place on the southern border of the promised land, near the Brook of Egypt.
azmon_130.today: Exact site unknown; possibly in the northeastern Sinai Peninsula.
key: The southern boundary turns from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passes along to Azmon (Joshua 15).
